mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60d returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate margins, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces revenue prospects for industrial firms and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60d returns are not significantly negative during four-month INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 2% for two months signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% AND CPIAUCSL > 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed 2% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-over-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 10% signals a collapse in residential investment, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d returns are not significantly negative when HOUST declines by more than 10% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A positive year-over-year change in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 1% combined with a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% signals a tight labor market, which raises wage pressures and cost of capital, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days in an expansionary regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60d returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS grows >1% YoY and UNRATE falls below 5% in an expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings and reduced consumer spending, which depresses corporate earnings and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS rises for three consecutive months.
